Kubernetes, for Software Engineers

For Software Engineers

Kubernetes reconciles desired state with actual state: a Deployment owns a ReplicaSet, the ReplicaSet keeps Pods alive, the Scheduler places them on Nodes, and a Service routes traffic to them.

    Your role

    Why this matters for a software engineer

    • Debug from the object model: Deployment, ReplicaSet, Pod, Node, and Service.
    • Interpret Pending Pods as a scheduling, capacity, or placement-constraint signal.
    • Expect controllers to recreate deleted resources when desired state still requires them.
    • Use the API Server as the control-plane boundary for kubectl, CI, and automation.

    How the pieces fit

    • Deployment owns ReplicaSet; ReplicaSet owns Pods.
    • Scheduler binds Pods to Nodes.
    • Service selects Pods independently of ownership.

    Useful debugging boundaries

    • Accepted spec but no Pod: inspect controllers and events.
    • Pending Pod: inspect requests, capacity, taints, and affinity.
    • Healthy Pod but no traffic: inspect Service selection and networking.

    Why this exists

    • Reconcile instead of scripting every recovery action.
    • Roll out and scale through desired state.
    • Decouple client addresses from ephemeral Pods.
